centralViewerQuestion: Why was crash driver Billy Bailey so severely disoriented on the Key West roadside, and what hidden criminal contraband inside his vehicle escalated a routine traffic check into a hospital escape and combative assault on officers?
hookPromise: Promises to uncover how an apparently dazed crash victim ended up tackled in a hospital parking lot while trying to flee police custody, and the shocking truth uncovered during his medical detox.

hookSelection.whyItWins: Candidate_016 captures the peak kinetic conflict where an officer tackles an escaped detainee onto the hospital parking lot asphalt at night, shouting commands and radioing dispatch. It provides immediate visual urgency and a massive curiosity gap (how did a crash victim end up fleeing a hospital in handcuffs?) while preserving spoiler boundaries. Candidate_021 was rejected because it features lower-stakes repetitive verbal arguing from a hospital bed. Candidate_001 was rejected because at 6.1s it is too brief and lacks visual/geographical context. Candidate_006 was rejected because an ambulance escort lacks urgent dramatic stakes.
hookSelection.hookTo15SecBridge: Following the 18-second parking lot takedown hook, narration executes a non-linear causal rewind: 'Hours before this chaotic hospital takedown, Key West 911 received reports of a violent single-car crash entering the city.' The visual immediately cuts to the downed streetlights and the driver sitting cross-legged on the curb.
